records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:157 — Calendar updates use the caller’s credentials, which cannot update the organizer’s event when the caller is an attendee; EventManager must use the organizer and their credentials.
records.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a real issue. In addGuests.handler.ts line 158, `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` fetches credentials for the requesting user (ctx.user), not the booking organizer. The EventManager is then initialized with these credentials at line 160-163. When an attendee (who has permission via isAttendee check at line 49) adds guests, the calendar update at line 165 `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` would use the attendee's credentials instead of the organizer's credentials. records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:164 — Concurrent guest additions can synchronize calendar attendee lists out of order, allowing an earlier request’s smaller snapshot to overwrite a later request’s complete list.
records.rationale: The finding describes a race condition in concurrent guest additions. Looking at addGuests.handler.ts, the handler: 1) reads booking with attendees (line 27-44), 2) filters unique guests based on current attendees (line 68-72), 3) creates new attendees (line 82-95), 4) calls eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking) (line 164). The evt.attendees list is built from the snapshot taken at step 1.
